correctness.rationale: For an acyclic precedence digraph, the intersection of all strict total-order extensions is exactly directed reachability, while a cycle gives inconsistent closure equal to all comparison attributes. Two-edge path and two-cycle premises are individually necessary for any complete iterative basis, and corresponding rules suffice. For one-round closure, simple directed paths of lengths 2 through n−1 and proper directed cycles of lengths 2 through n−1 are individually necessary; Hamiltonian cycles are handled by proper subpaths. Rule counts follow from labeled paths/cycles. Synchronous transitivity doubles known walk lengths per round; a directed Hamiltonian path proves the lower bound ceil(log2(n−1)). Actual verify.py independently tested 64 complete inputs n=3, 4096 complete inputs n=4, 1024 deterministic inputs n=5, cycle depth through n=8, all PASS. Finite checks are corroborative, not the general proof.
